The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. answers:
**[goal]** Single-file landing page `./landing/index.html` for Mondrian's *Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow* (1930), facts limited to `FACTSHEET.md`, in Mondrian's own visual language, openable directly in a browser that only reaches Google Fonts and the three.js CDN.

**[action]**
- Read `FACTSHEET.md`; built the page in one pass, then fixed three defects found by rendering it.
- Structure: masthead (title, kicker, byline: painter / year / movement / collection) → *The picture* (CSS-grid composition scheme + optional three.js relief) → *The movement* (De Stijl 1917, van Doesburg + Mondrian; four fact cards) → *Neoplasticism, three rules* (line / primary colour / non-colour swatches) → *Why it matters* → black *Read more at the source* block with the Wikipedia link, plus a footer note on scope.
- Visual language: red `#d40000`, blue `#0033a0`, yellow `#f7d300`, off-white ground, black 14px rules as section dividers and as the painting's dividing lines; Archivo / Archivo Black; the composition is drawn with a CSS grid (gaps = black lines), and the same scheme is rebuilt as a small three.js relief (flat `MeshBasicMaterial`, pointer parallax) inside `try { await import(...) }` so a blocked CDN leaves the page unchanged.
- Evidence loop: rendered with headless Edge (`--headless=new --screenshot`, virtual-time budget 9s) at 1280px, cropped regions with PIL, re-rendered after each fix. Headless instances exited on their own; the two `msedge.exe` entries still listed are pre-existing, not mine. Scratch screenshots in `tmp/` deleted; only `landing/index.html` added.

**[result]** `landing/index.html`, ~330 lines, no build step. Verified in rendered screenshots: composition scheme shows red square top right, blue square bottom left, yellow rectangle bottom right, white top left, thick black lines (first render had all cells white from a specificity bug, fixed with `.cells i.red`); relief shows the same scheme in true colour (was grey under lighting, fixed); fact-card body text on red/blue is now legible (was dark-on-dark); *Why it matters*, the yellow CTA to `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composition_with_Red,_Blue_and_Yellow`, and the footer all render, page ends cleanly at y=3413. Only external references are `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com` and the three.js CDN; Wikipedia appears only as the outbound source link.

Assumptions for what the brief left open: the page is in English; the "picture" is a labelled **scheme**, not a reproduction (the fact sheet gives no image rights or file), stated in the caption and footer; the three.js relief is decorative and optional, since the brief only guarantees the CDN is reachable; interpretive lines are paraphrase-level only ("balance here is not symmetry", "the movement's programme carried out to the letter", "left the studio and turned into a general layout language") and derive from the sheet's "asymmetric balance" and "reference for modern graphic design and architecture". No dates, dimensions, ownership history or provenance beyond the sheet are claimed.

**[next]** Optional: swap the scheme for a rights-cleared reproduction if one becomes available, and add a grey field to the Neoplasticism demo row if you want the non-colours shown in the painting itself rather than in the rules section.
